rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-year (2013<U+2013>2016) greenhouse field experiment, 4 treatments x 3 replicates, cucumber-celery rotation, Beijing. Q2: Table 3 and Results 'Vegetable yields, NUE and IWUE' <U+2013> RFPD (drip fertigation with 40% less urea-N) maintained or increased mean annual cucumber (100 vs 96 t/ha) and celery (97 vs 94 t/ha) yield relative to FP; Table 4 <U+2013> RFPD raised mean annual NUE (PFP) by 25% and IWUE by 40%; Table 2 <U+2013> RFPD cut annual N2O by 45%. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> only one fruit-leafy cropping pattern at one NCP site studied, larger-scale application needs verification by multi-year monitoring of other patterns; other N loss pathways not measured; Discussion notes low temporal resolution of moisture monitoring. Q9: Table 3 <U+2013> yields reported as means <U+00B1> standard errors of three replicates (e.g. cucumber RFPD 100 <U+00B1> 1, celery 97 <U+00B1> 2).
rows.notes: Claim overstates: the study says yields were 'maintained' (cucumber RFPD vs FP not significantly different, letters ab vs b; celery significantly higher), not that drip+reduced N 'significantly improved' yield overall. Comparison RFPD vs FP confounds drip with N reduction, but FPD treatment isolates drip. Q3: single method (plot yield weighing). Q4: WFPS and soil mineral N were measured but not analysed as the mechanism for yield; the yield mechanism (meeting plant N/water needs) is inferred, so 'no'. Q5: one site, one soil, two crops. Q7: no stated requirement for the yield effect; the note that recommended N rate should consider initial soil N is generic.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-year replicated greenhouse field experiment in Beijing. Q2: Table 4 and Results 'Vegetable yields, NUE and IWUE' <U+2013> IWUE under drip fertigation (FPD, RFPD) significantly higher than under flood (FP) in every season; FPD and RFPD increased mean annual IWUE by 37% and 40% (44 and 45 vs 32 kg/m3); Table 1 <U+2013> drip treatments received 20<U+2013>40% less irrigation water. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> only one cropping pattern at one NCP site, regional/national application needs verification; other N loss pathways unknown.
rows.notes: IWUE = yield / irrigation volume; the water saving is a management-imposed lower irrigation volume under drip (Table 1) with maintained yield. Q3: one method. Q4: soil WFPS and irrigation volume recorded, but no measurement of the mechanism (e.g. evaporation, drainage) by which drip raised IWUE. Q5: single site/soil, two crops. Q7: no stated condition for the IWUE effect. Q9: Table 4 gives IWUE means with letter groupings only, no SD/SE/CI (N2O and yield tables do have SE, but IWUE does not).

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-year field experiment with 4 treatments x 3 replicates in a Beijing greenhouse. Q2: Table 4 and Abstract <U+2013> RFPD (drip fertigation with ~40% less urea-N) improved mean annual IWUE by 40% and NUE by 25% vs FP; Table 2 <U+2013> mean annual N2O reduced by ~45%; Table 3 <U+2013> celery mean annual yield 97 vs 94 t/ha (maintained/increased). Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> single cropping pattern and site, larger-scale application needs verification, other N loss pathways not quantified.
rows.notes: Passage matches the study's reported RFPD-vs-FP figures. Note RFPD vs FP compares drip+reduced N against flood+conventional N, so the 40% IWUE gain reflects drip (FPD alone gave 37%) rather than N reduction. Q3: one method. Q4: no mechanistic measurement for the IWUE effect. Q5: one site. Q7: no stated requirement. Q9: Table 4 IWUE values lack any dispersion measure.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-year replicated greenhouse experiment. Q2: Table 3 and Results <U+2013> RFPD significantly enhanced mean annual celery yield (97 vs 94 t/ha for FP) and did not reduce cucumber yield, i.e. reducing synthetic N by 40% under drip had no negative yield impact; Table 4 <U+2013> NUE +25%, IWUE +40%; Table 2 <U+2013> N2O <U+2212>45%. Q8: 'Study limitation and future perspectives' <U+2013> results from one cropping pattern at one NCP site, scaling needs verification; yield gap in CK only appeared from S4 due to high initial soil N, so recommended N rate depends on initial soil conditions. Q9: Table 3 <U+2013> yields given as mean <U+00B1> standard error of three replicates.
rows.notes: Study supports the claim. Q3: single method. Q4: WFPS and soil mineral N measured but not linked to yield mechanism. Q5: one site/soil, two crops. Q7: the statement that N recommendations should account for planting conditions and initial soil N is close to a support factor but is framed as a general recommendation about N rate, not a stated requirement for drip to deliver yield; answered no.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-site, three-year plot experiment (12 plots of 8 m x 6 m) in one greenhouse in Beijing; drip fertigation effects are isolated by FPD vs FP, while RFPD vs FP combines drip with 40% synthetic-N reduction. Dispersion (SE) reported for N2O and yields but not for IWUE/NUE.
